newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Wallis sees clear advice on bank ownership.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Wallis sees clear advice on bank ownership.

text.p: The Australian government's inquiry into the financial system is likely to make a "black and white" recommendation on foreign ownership in the sector, inquiry chairman Stan Wallis said on Thursday.
Asked by reporters following a speech if he expected to make a fairly strong recommendation on the issue, he said: "I suspect it is going to be one of the black and white ones, yes."
"It is clearly a hot issue, we have got a very even sort of split, I would suspect, about it," he said.

"There are those that are absolutely against it philosophically, there are those against it in the sense that the financial system should remain as relatively free of foreign ownership as is possible and those who believe clearly it is a global market place," he said.
Wallis said he did not believe the federal government would need to address taxation reform as a result of the inquiry.
"Not necessarily, no. I think the government has got a very clear view about where they are going on tax reform," he said.
"But it clearly is reasonable for us to bring out any issues of a taxation nature if they are relevant to what our terms of reference are and that is all we will be doing," he said.
Wallis had been addressing the Australian Institute of Company Directors following the hearing of public submissions to the inquiry in Adelaide.
